relevance_reason: Paper that identified mutations in SLC25A38 as the cause of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia (SIDBA2).

findings.statement: By positional cloning, Guernsey et al. (2009) identified mutations in the SLC25A38 gene, which encodes an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein, in patients with a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.
quotes: by positional cloning, we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38

findings.statement: Guernsey et al. (2009) noted that the sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematologic disorders whose morphologic hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts, bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria.
quotes: The sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematological disorders whose morphological hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts--bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count

findings.statement: Guernsey et al. (2009) demonstrated that SLC25A38 is important for the biosynthesis of heme in eukaryotes.
quotes: demonstrate that SLC25A38 is important for the biosynthesis of heme in eukaryotes

relevance_reason: Describes a sib pair with pyridoxine-refractory congenital sideroblastic anemia, with linkage to ALAS2 excluded and evidence supporting autosomal recessive inheritance.

findings.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) reported a brother and sister, born to unaffected parents, who had transfusion-dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia from birth. Their hemoglobin levels were 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl, respectively.
quotes: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth. Their haemoglobin levels were 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl, respectively.

findings.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) found that delta-aminolevulinate synthase activity in erythroblasts from fractionated marrow of the affected sister was 135 pmol ALA formed/10(6) erythroblasts/hour, within the normal range of 110-650 pmol.
quotes: delta-Aminolaevulinate synthase activity in erythroblasts from fractionated marrow of the sister was 135 pmol delta-aminolaevulinate formed/10(6) erythroblasts/hour (normal range = 110-650 pmol).

findings.statement: In the affected son, Jardine et al. (1994) found no mutations in the ALAS2 gene on sequence analysis of the coding region, the intron/exon boundaries, or the 1-kb 5-prime promoter region.
quotes: sequence analysis of the ALAS2 gene in the son did not identify any mutations in the coding region, the intron/exon boundaries, or the 1 kb 5' promoter region.

findings.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) identified a G-to-A polymorphism 220 nt 3-prime of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal of ALAS2, with a gene frequency of 25% in 148 alleles. Analysis of this intragenic polymorphism showed that the affected sibs had received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus, which excluded ALAS2 mutations as the cause of their sideroblastic anemia.
quotes: A useful polymorphism was found in the 3' region of the ALAS2 gene, a G to A transition, 220 nt 3' of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal.

Analysis of the inheritance of this intragenic polymorphism showed that the affected sibs received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus, excluding mutations in this gene as the cause of their sideroblastic anaemia.

findings.statement: Jardine et al. (1994) found that the mother of the affected sibs had no dimorphic erythrocyte population and showed random X inactivation in peripheral leukocytes, which indicated that she did not carry an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation. The authors concluded that the results strongly suggested autosomal recessive inheritance in this family.
quotes: the absence of a dimorphic erythrocyte population in the mother, coupled with the demonstration of random X inactivation in her peripheral leucocytes, showed that the mother was not the carrier of any X linked sideroblastic anaemia mutation.
These results strongly suggest that the sideroblastic anaemia in this family is an autosomal recessive trait.

relevance_reason: The paper is a case report of a female infant with congenital sideroblastic anemia that did not respond to pyridoxine, with biochemical studies of ALA synthetase.

findings.statement: Manabe et al. (1982) described a female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia that did not respond to pyridoxine therapy.
quotes: A female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia is described.
which could explain the unresponsiveness to pyridoxine therapy in this case

findings.statement: Manabe et al. (1982) found markedly reduced delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity in erythroblasts from the patient, both with and without pyridoxal phosphate treatment. Activity of erythroblast mitochondrial neutral protease, which specifically inactivates the apo form of ALA synthetase, was normal, and the apoenzyme's sensitivity to the protease was also normal. The authors speculated that the reduced ALA synthetase activity resulted from impaired production of the enzyme rather than faster breakdown, which could explain why the patient did not respond to pyridoxine.
quotes: A marked reduction of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity of erythroblasts was noticed with and without treatment of pyridoxal phosphate.

Mitochondrial neutral protease activity of erythroblasts, which inactivates specifically the apo form of ALA synthetase, was normal and the sensitivity of apo form of ALA synthetase to the neutral protease was also normal.
It was speculated that the reduction of ALA synthetase activity is not due to the high speed of destruction, but rather due to the impairment in production of ALA synthetase
